newsitem.title: MEXICO: Latam stocks seen unsettled by volatile U.S. mkts.
newsitem.headline: Latam stocks seen unsettled by volatile U.S. mkts.

text.p: Investors can expect a rough ride in most Latin American stock markets this week on the back of unsettled U.S. stock and bond markets, analysts and dealers said.
Only Brazil's Sao Paulo bourse has upside potential on optimism that a constitutional amendment allowing presidential re-election will pass in Congress' lower house this week, analysts said.
Last week the Bovespa index lost 0.7 percent to end at 77,598 points.
Analysts said, however, investors should take into account volatility in U.S. stock prices as a factor weighing on the local market.
"If Wall Street remains volatile, local shares could suffer," a senior trader said.
Mexican stocks are seen closely watching developments on Wall Street and U.S. bond market reaction to U.S. economic indicators in the run-up to the February 4 Federal Open Market Committee Meeting.

"Although the Fed is not expected to change interest rates, there is always volatility and nervousness before FOMC meetings," said Esteban Rojas, deputy director of analysis at the Arka brokerage in Mexico City.
On the home front, Rojas saw Mexican equity prices churning as fund managers reshuffle portfolios in the wake of the first Q4 earnings reports now being posted.
The blue chip IPC index ended a record-breaking New Year rally to close the week 1.43 percent down on Friday at 3,733.16 points.

Argentine stocks are expected to continue to closely track Wall Street this week, although company results due to be released over the next few days could help temper any new selling bout, dealers said.
"If the markets in New York are as volatile as they were last Thursday and Friday we will probably be in for a bumpy ride," said Jose Napoli of brokers Ignoto y Napoli.
The blue-chip MerVal index snapped a five-week rally and closed 2.8 percent lower at 661.95 last week on the heels of the Wall Street selloff. The weekly drop pared January gains to 1.9 percent.

After a string a heavy losses last week, Chilean stocks are seen remaining unsettled with the market undermined by fears over the impact of this year's drought on the power sector and continuing high interest rates, traders said.
"Once again this makes the end of the adjustment even more distant," said one dealer referring to the central bank's tight monetary policy.
The tumbled 4.28 percent last week to close at 108.35 points.
Caracas stocks are seen flat in sluggish trade as investors continue to wait out the resolution of on-going labor strife before returning to the market, analysts said.
"There's a wait-and-see feeling among foreign investors, which they can afford after last year's gains," said New York based IDEA analyst Gene Frieda.
The bolsa's leading 19-share index closed Friday at 6,253.12 points, off 3.3 percent on the week.
